## Modular Neuro-Symbolic App Architecture

`specshiny` ships three composable `bslib`/Shiny modules that share a single
reactive source of truth (`spec_rv`, holding a validated `spec_ir`) and a
change-diff channel (`last_diff_rv`, holding the latest `spec_diff`):

| Module | Role |
| :--- | :--- |
| `mod_spec_composer_ui()` / `mod_spec_composer_server()` | Natural-language prompt compilation, presets, iterative conversational refinement, clarification questions, and defaults rationale viewer |
| `mod_spec_controls_ui()` / `mod_spec_controls_server()` | Dynamically renders *only* active `bslib` controls, pushes IR changes to widgets, validates UI edits through guardrails, and renders visual diff badges |
| `mod_spec_preview_ui()` / `mod_spec_preview_server()` | Live mathematical summary, YAML/JSON IR inspector, deterministic R script, quick preview runner, Quarto `.qmd` report, and download handlers |

## 1. Launching the Bundled Flagship Demo

The fastest way to explore the complete workflow interactively is to run the
bundled reference application:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
library(specshiny)
run_specshiny_demo()
```

Or inspect the `shiny.appobj` directly:

```{r}
library(specshiny)
app <- specshiny_demo_app()
class(app)
```

## 2. Composing a Custom `bslib` Application

Embedding `specshiny` inside your own `bslib` dashboard requires only wiring
the shared `reactiveVal` pair across the modules:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
library(shiny)
library(bslib)
library(specshiny)

# Swap translator_rule() for translator_openai() or translator_ollama() when desired
translator <- translator_rule()
initial <- nl_to_spec(
  "2-level power study with 50 schools, 20 students per school, ICC 0.2, treatment effect 0.4",
  translator = translator
)$spec

ui <- page_sidebar(
  title = "Custom Multilevel Study Studio",
  theme = bs_theme(version = 5, bootswatch = "flatly"),
  sidebar = sidebar(
    width = 380,
    mod_spec_composer_ui("composer")
  ),
  layout_columns(
    col_widths = c(6, 6),
    mod_spec_controls_ui("controls"),
    mod_spec_preview_ui("preview")
  )
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  spec_rv <- reactiveVal(initial)
  last_diff_rv <- reactiveVal(NULL)

  mod_spec_composer_server("composer", spec_rv = spec_rv, translator = translator, last_diff_rv = last_diff_rv)
  mod_spec_controls_server("controls", spec_rv = spec_rv, last_diff_rv = last_diff_rv)
  mod_spec_preview_server("preview", spec_rv = spec_rv, last_diff_rv = last_diff_rv)
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

## 3. Verifying Bidirectional Sync with `shiny::testServer()`

Because all state transitions pass through validated `spec_ir` objects and
idempotent diff checks, bidirectional synchronization between conversational
refinements and visual widget tweaks is straightforward to test automatically
with `shiny::testServer()`:

```{r}
init_spec <- nl_to_spec(
  "2-level power study with 50 schools, 20 students per school, ICC 0.2, treatment effect 0.35, random slope for x1, 15% MAR missingness"
)$spec

spec_rv <- shiny::reactiveVal(init_spec)
diff_rv <- shiny::reactiveVal(NULL)

shiny::testServer(
  mod_spec_controls_server,
  args = list(spec_rv = spec_rv, last_diff_rv = diff_rv),
  {
    # 1. Visual slider/numeric tweak updates IR and populates semantic diff
    session$setInputs(n_clusters = 75)
    cat("After UI tweak -> n_clusters:", spec_rv()$hierarchy$n_clusters, "\n")
    cat("Live diff summary:", format_diff_summary(diff_rv()), "\n")

    # 2. Invalid edit (cluster_size = 2 with 2 random effects) is blocked by guardrails
    session$setInputs(cluster_size = 2)
    cat("Blocked edit kept cluster_size at:", spec_rv()$hierarchy$cluster_size, "\n")
    cat("Guardrail message:", session$returned$guardrail_error()$errors$message[[1L]], "\n")

    # 3. Structural edit (turning off missingness) immediately prunes missingness controls
    session$setInputs(missing_mechanism = "none")
    cat("Missingness rate control still present?",
        "missing_rate" %in% session$returned$descriptor()$control_ids, "\n")

    # 4. Undo reverts missingness back to MAR cleanly
    session$setInputs(undo_btn = 1)
    cat("After Undo -> missingness mechanism:", spec_rv()$missingness$mechanism, "\n")
  }
)
```

## 3b. Interactive Preview Budget Guardrails

`mod_spec_preview_server()` enforces configurable iteration, sample-size, and
wall-clock caps (`max_preview_reps`, `max_preview_n`, `max_preview_seconds`)
so large simulation designs (e.g., `n_reps = 50000`) never freeze the Shiny
event loop while preserving the full specification in downloaded `.R` scripts:

```{r}
large_spec <- new_spec_ir(
  design_type = "monte_carlo_lm",
  hierarchy = list(levels = 1L, n_obs = 5000L),
  simulation = list(n_reps = 50000L, seed = 2026L)
)
large_rv <- shiny::reactiveVal(large_spec)

shiny::testServer(
  mod_spec_preview_server,
  args = list(spec_rv = large_rv, max_preview_reps = 5L, max_preview_n = 500L),
  {
    session$setInputs(run_preview = 1)
    print(session$returned$preview_results())
    cat("Warnings:", paste(session$returned$preview_warnings(), collapse = " | "), "\n")
  }
)
```

## 4. Configuring Cloud & Local LLM Translators

`specshiny` supports any OpenAI-compatible API (`translator_openai()`) as well
as local Ollama models (`translator_ollama()`). Both adapters enforce JSON-only
output using `spec_system_prompt()`, parse the JSON strictly with
`jsonlite::fromJSON()` (never `eval(parse())`), and validate every returned
specification through `validate_spec_ir()`:

```{r}
# Cloud API backend (reads OPENAI_API_KEY from environment by default)
openai_backend <- translator_openai(model = "gpt-4o-mini")
openai_backend

# Local privacy-preserving Ollama backend
ollama_backend <- translator_ollama(model = "llama3.1", base_url = "http://localhost:11434")
ollama_backend
```

To inspect the exact schema instructions sent to external LLMs:

```{r}
cat(spec_system_prompt("create"))
```
